title: SB2265 (2018 Regular): RELATING TO FIREARMS.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Hawaii) (gun-policy Stage 5, Hawaii); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Hawaii text (Introduced, official copy, https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2018/bills/SB2265_.HTM; sha256 b127e0cd77865174e86990535458a6ae9f5353621fe88ea289d00d82cf652372)
provenance.note: As-filed text (introduced). In HRS 134-8 the bill relists the existing prohibited items as a numbered list (1)-(8) and adds items (9)-(12); the quotes give the intro sentence and the added items, each line a separate part.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (HRS 134-3): Any registration under this section shall expire five years from the date the registration is issued or December 31, 2023, whichever is later.
SECTION 1 (HRS 134-3): The registration renewal shall be on forms prescribed by the attorney general, which shall be uniform throughout the State, and shall include the same information as the registration.
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-8): The manufacture, possession, sale, barter, trade, gift, transfer, or acquisition of any of the following is prohibited:
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-8): (9) Bump stocks, gat cranks, or any devices that can allow a person to manipulate the trigger mechanism of a firearm more rapidly than the person could without the device;
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-8): (10) Firearm trigger mechanisms that have been replaced or modified to have a lighter trigger-pull than the trigger mechanism installed in the firearm by the manufacturer;
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-8): (11) Flash suppressers or any devices that reduce the visible signature of a firearm's discharge; and
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-8): (12) Any type of firearm modification that significantly increases the amount of time that a firearm may be continuously operated before the firearm overheats.
